reading: Every solid square loses its outer ring (side n becomes n-2, placed one cell in from its top-left); a single cell instead grows into a 9x9 square (rows r-4..r+4, cols c-5..c+3). A 7x8 box became 5x5, so the new side is min(h,w)-2.
verb: shrink squares one ring, grow single cells to 9x9
why: every object in the output is the input object resized along the cycle 9->7->5->3->1->9; background elsewhere

reading: The two leftmost columns of every object are erased to background; objects only two wide disappear.
verb: erase leftmost two columns of each object

new_rows.name: left2
new_rows.datalog:
minx(O, min(X)) :- obj(O, Y, X), cell(Y, X, C).
left2(Y, X) :- obj(O, Y, X), cell(Y, X, C), minx(O, M), L = M + 2, X < L.

why: every cell in the first two columns of its object becomes 8 (the background); nothing else changes
invariants: all cells right of each object's second column

reading: Two overlapping objects swap layering: in the overlap cells the colour of the object that was on top is replaced by the colour of the object that was underneath.

slots.subject: cells where two straight-edged objects (rectangles/lines) overlap
slots.colour: the colour of the occluded object (the one whose shape continues through the overlap)

why: only overlap cells change, and each takes the other object's colour

reading: Each yellow rectangle containing k dots of one colour gets a surrounding border of width k in that dot colour.
verb: frame each rectangle, width = dot count

slots.subject: each 4-coloured rectangle with inner dots
slots.colour: the colour of its inner dots

why: around every rectangle the ring of thickness k (k = its dot count) is painted the dot colour; rectangle itself unchanged

reading: Plus shapes whose centres lie on a common diagonal are joined by a diagonal line of colour 2 through the background cells between them.

new_rows.name: diagjoin
new_rows.datalog:
centre(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), Ya = Y - 1, Yb = Y + 1, Xa = X - 1, Xb = X + 1, cell(Ya, X, C1), cell(Yb, X, C2), cell(Y, Xa, C3), cell(Y, Xb, C4).
bgc(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C).
diagjoin(Y, X) :- centre(Y1, X1), centre(Y2, X2), E = Y2 - Y1, F = X2 - X1, E = F, E > 0, bgc(Y, X), DY = Y - Y1, DX = X - X1, DY = DX, DY > 0, DY < E.
diagjoin(Y, X) :- centre(Y1, X1), centre(Y2, X2), E = Y2 - Y1, F = X1 - X2, E = F, E > 0, bgc(Y, X), DY = Y - Y1, DX = X1 - X, DY = DX, DY > 0, DY < E.

why: every background cell strictly between two diagonally aligned plus centres becomes 2; nothing else changes
invariants: plus pairs on the same row/column or off-diagonal are not joined

reading: Each bar standing on the bottom edge is lifted straight up by its own height.
verb: lift each object by its height
why: every object keeps shape and colour and its new top row = old top row minus its height

reading: The whole 3x3 grid is painted with the input's most frequent colour.

slots.colour: the most common colour of the input

why: every output cell equals the mode colour of the input

reading: Each 9-coloured core stays put; every other object touching a core is pushed away from it in the direction of the side it touches, until it reaches the grid edge.
verb: push attached pieces away from the core to the edge

slots.subject: each non-9 object orthogonally attached to a core
slots.direction: away from the core cell it touches (up/down/left/right)

why: every moved object keeps its shape and ends touching the border on the side opposite the core; pieces already at the border stay

reading: The green shape slides toward the red wall until it touches it, then a full line of 8 is drawn just beyond the shape on the side away from the wall.
verb: slide to wall and cap with 8 line

new_rows.name: cap
new_rows.datalog:
bgc(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C).
rowgap(Y) :- bgc(Y, X).
colgap(X) :- bgc(Y, X).
fullrow(Y) :- cell(Y, X, C), !rowgap(Y).
fullcol(X) :- cell(Y, X, C), !colgap(X).
shp(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), !fullrow(Y), !fullcol(X).
shminy(min(Y)) :- shp(Y, X).
shmaxy(max(Y)) :- shp(Y, X).
shminx(min(X)) :- shp(Y, X).
shmaxx(max(X)) :- shp(Y, X).
cap(Y, X) :- fullrow(S), shmaxy(M), M < S, shminy(N), Y = N - 1, px(Y, X, C).
cap(Y, X) :- fullrow(S), shminy(N), N > S, shmaxy(M), Y = M + 1, px(Y, X, C).
cap(Y, X) :- fullcol(S), shmaxx(M), M < S, shminx(N), X = N - 1, px(Y, X, C).
cap(Y, X) :- fullcol(S), shminx(N), N > S, shmaxx(M), X = M + 1, px(Y, X, C).

why: the shape keeps its form and ends in contact with the 2 line; the row/column adjacent to the shape on the far side becomes all 8

reading: A 2x2 colour key sits in a corner behind 8 borders; every dot in the square field is recoloured with the key colour of the field quadrant it lies in.

slots.key: the 2x2 block of colours in the corner outside the 8 border
slots.subject: the dots in the 0-background field
slots.colour: key cell (i,j) for the dot in field quadrant (i,j) (field halves by row and column)

why: each dot's new colour is the key entry matching its quadrant of the field; key, 8 border and background unchanged
